pipeline.attack_summary: Slingshot is a sophisticated APT malware platform that initially compromises Mikrotik routers via Winbox Loader, downloading malicious DLLs like ipv4.dll to infect administrators' machines. It uses kernel-mode modules such as Cahnadr/NDriver and user-mode GollumApp for persistence, data exfiltration, and credential access, leveraging vulnerable drivers to bypass security controls.

indicators.context: The initial loader replaces the victim's legitimate Windows library 'scesrv.dll' with a malicious one of exactly the same size.
This turned out to be a malicious loader internally named 'Slingshot', part of a new, and highly sophisticated attack platform.
Following infection, Slingshot would load a number of modules onto the victim device, including two huge and powerful ones: Cahnadr, the kernel mode module.
Canhadr, also known as NDriver, contains low-level routines for network, IO operations and so on.
GollumApp, a user mode module. The two modules are connected and able to support each other in information gathering, persistence and data exfiltration.
One of them – ipv4.dll – has been placed by the APT with what is, in fact, a downloader for other malicious components.

In turn, this infected the administrator of the router. We were able to find several cases where the attackers got access to Mikrotik routers and placed a component downloaded by Winbox Loader, a management suite for Mikrotik routers.
We were able to find several cases where the attackers got access to Mikrotik routers and placed a component downloaded by Winbox Loader, a management suite for Mikrotik routers.
During our research we also found a component called KPWS that turned out to be another downloader for Slingshot components.
These vulnerabilities include CVE-2007-5633; CVE-2010-1592, CVE-2009-0824.

pipeline.attack_summary: An attacker uses phishing emails containing malicious links to deliver a NetWire RAT variant. The initial payload is a 7z archive that extracts to an EXE file named 'PROFORMA-INVOICE 0990.exe'. This malware employs anti-analysis techniques like dynamic code extraction and anti-sandboxing, then establishes persistence via registry keys and auto-run entries. It communicates with a C2 server (gbam0001.duckdns.org) to send collected data including system information, keystrokes, and credentials.

Ransomware was also deployed as a decoy to distract from the destructive wiper attacks.

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via GRIFFON Implant Execution with wscript.exe or msutil.exe
id: 5a6e8b9c-1f2d-4e3a-9b4c-7a8d9e0f1a2b
status: experimental
description: Detects initial access via malicious Office documents that execute GRIFFON implant using wscript.exe or copied variants like mses.exe/msutil.exe, which are indicators of FIN7 spearphishing campaigns.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/fin7-5-the-infamous-cybercrime-rig-fin7-continues-its-activities/90703/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1587/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-06
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_process:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\mses.exe'
            - '\msutil.exe'
            - '\sctasks.exe'
    selection_cmdline:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'Errors.txt'
            - 'Errors.bat'
    condition: all of selection_*/**
falsepositives:

level: high

id: fc65612a-64c2-47ae-abec-391b8cc84ea7
status: experimental
description: Detects execution of PowerShell with obfuscated command line arguments commonly used by FIN7 to execute GRIFFON implant, including -NoP -NonI -ExecutionPolicy Bypass.

author: Sigma Assistant

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'

            - '-NonI'

falsepositives:

title: Persistence via GRIFFON Implant Registry Key Modification
id: 5d5dcab4-d58e-4583-aedb-b0a4de2ca94b
status: experimental
description: Detects persistence mechanism used by GRIFFON implant through registry modifications using Task* naming convention, which is a common pattern for FIN7 implants.
references:
    - https://securelist.com/fin7-5-the-infamous-cybercrime-rig-fin7-continues-its-activities/90703/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1587/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-06
tags:
    - attack.persistence
    - attack.t1547.001
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_registry:
        TargetObject|contains: \SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run\
    selection_taskname:
        Details|contains:
            - 'TaskbyzNne'
            - 'Taskc9FGG'
            - 'TaskzEsb'
    condition: all of selection_*/**
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate software using similar registry keys
    - System maintenance tools that create scheduled tasks
level: high

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via CVE-2023-22518 Confluence Exploitation Attempt
id: 5e6a7b8c-9d4f-4e5a-b678-1234567890ab
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects the initial access phase of CVE-2023-22518 exploitation attempt against Atlassian Confluence.
    It identifies unauthenticated POST requests to /json/setup-restore.action with X-Atlassian-Token: no-check header,
    and a multipart form data payload containing a .zip file, which is used to reset the application and create an admin account.
references:
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/security/cve-2023-22518-improper-authorization-vulnerability-in-confluence-data-center-and-server-1311473907.html
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/confluence-to-cerber-exploitation-of-cve-2023-22518-for-ransomware-deployment
    - https://github.com/ForceFledgling/CVE-2023-22518
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.t1548.002
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_method:
        cs-method: POST
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-stem: /json/setup-restore.action
    selection_header:
        cs-header: X-Atlassian-Token: no-check
    selection_content_type:
        cs-header|contains: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary
    selection_body:
        cs-body|contains:
            - file";filename=".*\.zip
            - buildIndex=true
            - edit=Upload and import
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts or tools using the same endpoint with valid authentication
level: critical

title: Privilege Escalation via CVE-2023-22518 Confluence Authentication Bypass
id: 6f7b8c9d-0e5f-1a6b-7c8d-2345678901ab
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule identifies privilege escalation attempts through CVE-2023-22518 where attackers attempt to bypass authentication
    and reset Confluence to create an administrator account. It looks for POST requests to known vulnerable endpoints with
    the X-Atlassian-Token: no-check header and multipart form data containing a .zip file.

    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/security/cve-2023-22518-improper-authorization-vulnerability-in-confluence-data-center-and-server-1311473907.html
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/confluence-to-cerber-exploitation-of-cve-2023-22518-for-ransomware-deployment
    - https://github.com/ForceFledgling/CVE-2023-22518
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1548/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.privilege-escalation
    - attack.t1548.002
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_method:
        cs-method: POST
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-stem:
            - /json/setup-restore.action
            - /json/setup-restore-local.action
            - /json/setup-restore-progress.action
    selection_header:
        cs-header: X-Atlassian-Token: no-check
    selection_content_type:
        cs-header|contains: multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary
    selection_body:
        cs-body|contains:
            - file";filename=".*\.zip
            - buildIndex=true
            - edit=Upload and import
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts or tools using the same endpoint with valid authentication
level: critical

title: Execution of PowerShell Commands Post-CVE-2023-22518 Exploitation
id: de940abe-14c6-4367-bfc6-427d78ee39e3
status: experimental
description: |
    This rule detects execution of PowerShell commands used in post-exploitation after gaining administrative access via CVE-2023-22518.
    It identifies the use of PowerShell.exe with command-line arguments indicative of downloading and executing malicious payloads,
    such as those associated with Cerber ransomware deployment.
references:
    - https://confluence.atlassian.com/security/cve-2023-22518-improper-authorization-vulnerability-in-confluence-data-center-and-server-1311473907.html
    - https://www.huntress.com/blog/confluence-to-cerber-exploitation-of-cve-2023-22518-for-ransomware-deployment
    - https://github.com/ForceFledgling/CVE-2023-22518
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1490/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.impact
    - attack.t1490
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_img:
        Image|endswith: \powershell.exe
    selection_cmdline:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'hXXp://193.176.179[.]41/tmp.37'
            - '-Command'
            - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
            - 'DownloadString'
    condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative scripts using PowerShell for system management
level: high

The first attack used wAgent malware, deployed via command-line execution with rundll32.exe using a 16-byte AES key parameter to decrypt payloads. The second attack used Bookcode malware in a supply chain attack against the pharmaceutical company. Both attacks leveraged persistence mechanisms through Windows services and Security Support Providers, and included credential access techniques such as SAM dumping.

rules_yaml:
title: Initial Access via CVE-2021-44077 in ManageEngine SupportCenter Plus
id: 5a6e8b3c-9d4f-4a2b-8c1d-7e9f6a4b2c8e
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects initial access via unauthenticated exploitation of CVE-2021-44077 in ManageEngine SupportCenter Plus by monitoring for HTTP POST requests to the /RestAPI/ImportTechnicians?step=1 endpoint, which is part of the exploit chain that uploads a PE file and triggers execution.
references:
    - https://thedfirreport.com/2022/06/06/will-the-real-msiexec-please-stand-up-exploit-leads-to-data-exfiltration/
    - https://github.com/horizon3ai/CVE-2021-44077/blob/b7a48e25824e8ead95e028475c7fd0e107e6e6bf/exploit.py
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1190/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.initial-access
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains: '/RestAPI/ImportTechnicians?step=1'
        cs-method: POST
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative uploads to the ImportTechnicians endpoint (if any exist)
level: high

title: Execution of MSI Agent via CVE-2021-44077 Exploitation
id: 9f8d7c6b-5a4e-3b2c-1d0f-8e7c6b5a4d3e
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects execution of msiexec.exe with command line arguments indicating installation of a malicious Windows agent, as part of the CVE-2021-44077 exploit chain. This rule targets the second stage of exploitation where msiexec is invoked to install the payload.
references:
    - https://thedfirreport.com/2022/06/06/will-the-real-msiexec-please-stand-up-exploit-leads-to-data-exfiltration/
    - https://github.com/horizon3ai/CVE-2021-44077/blob/b7a48e25824e8ead95e028475c7fd0e107e6e6bf/exploit.py
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/007/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'msiexec.exe /i Site24x7WindowsAgent.msi'
            - '/qn'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate installations of Site24x7 Windows Agent or similar software
level: high

title: WDigest Registry Modification for Credential Access
id: 2b5c6d7e-8f9a-1b2c-3d4e-5f6a7b8c9d0e
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects modification of the WDigest registry key to enable credential caching, a technique used in post-exploitation after CVE-2021-44077 exploitation to dump LSASS credentials.
references:
    - https://thedfirreport.com/2022/06/06/will-the-real-msiexec-please-stand-up-exploit-leads-to-data-exfiltration/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1112/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1003/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.credential-access
    - attack.defense-evasion
    - attack.t1112
    - attack.t1003.001
logsource:
    category: registry_set
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains: 'HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurityProviders\WDigest\UseLogonCredential'
        Details|contains: '1'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - System or security tool configurations enabling WDigest
level: high

title: Discovery Activity via CVE-2021-44077 Webshell
id: 7c8d9e0f-1a2b-3c4d-5e6f-7a8b9c0d1e2f
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects discovery commands executed via the fm2.jsp webshell, a common post-exploitation activity after CVE-2021-44077 exploitation. These commands include systeminfo, tasklist, and arp -a to gather system information.
references:
    - https://thedfirreport.com/2022/06/06/will-the-real-msiexec-please-stand-up-exploit-leads-to-data-exfiltration/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1057/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1012/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.t1057
    - attack.t1012
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - 'cmd=systeminfo'
            - 'cmd=tasklist'
            - 'cmd=arp -a'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative monitoring using similar commands
level: medium

title: Lateral Movement via SSH Tunneling for RDP Proxying
id: 3d4e5f6a-7b8c-9d0e-1f2a-3b4c5d6e7f8a
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects lateral movement using SSH tunneling via Plink to proxy RDP connections, a technique used after exploitation of CVE-2021-44077. This rule targets the command line that sets up the tunnel.
references:
    - https://thedfirreport.com/2022/06/06/will-the-real-msiexec-please-stand-up-exploit-leads-to-data-exfiltration/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.lateral-movement
    - attack.command-and-control
    - attack.t1572
    - attack.t1021.001
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'echo y|'
            - '-ssh'
            - '-R'
            - ':443'
            - ':3389'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of SSH tunneling tools for authorized access
level: high

title: File Enumeration via CVE-2021-44077 Webshell
id: 8e9f0a1b-2c3d-4e5f-6a7b-8c9d0e1f2a3b
status: experimental
description: |
    Detects file enumeration commands executed via the fm2.jsp webshell, indicating potential exfiltration activity after exploitation of CVE-2021-44077. These commands target various system directories to gather files.
references:
    - https://thedfirreport.com/2022/06/06/will-the-real-msiexec-please-stand-up-exploit-leads-to-data-exfiltration/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1087/002/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.t1087.002
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - 'p=C:/Windows/Temp'
            - 'p=C:/Windows'
            - 'p=C:/'
            - 'p=C:/ALLibraries'
            - 'p=C:/Users'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate administrative file system browsing
level: medium

description: Detects execution of PowerShell script through WMI to gather OS information during lateral movement, a technique used by FIN7 in Veeam exploitation campaigns.
references:
    - https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/fin7-target-veeam-servers
    - https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/fin7-target-veeam-servers/jcr:content/root/responsivegrid/responsivegrid/responsivegrid/image_253944286.img.png/1682500394900.png
    - https://github.com/WithSecureLabs/iocs/blob/344203de742bb7e68bd56618f66d34be95a9f9fc/FIN7VEEAM/iocs.csv
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1018/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-10-07
tags:
    - attack.discovery
    - attack.t1018
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
        CommandLine|contains: 'WMI'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate WMI-based PowerShell scripts
level: medium

validation_issues.message: The detection for sqlservr.exe executing shell commands is too generic and may produce false positives. Consider adding more specific indicators like command patterns or arguments.
Hardcoded IP address in network detection rule. While this may be accurate for the specific campaign, it reduces flexibility for future similar attacks.
The parent image check for gup.exe loading libcurl.dll is a good indicator of side-loading behavior. However, ensure that this detection does not conflict with legitimate usage.
Detection based on WMI in command line is valid but may be too broad. Consider adding more specific WMI queries or patterns to reduce false positives.
